newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ council mulls sell-down of Wellington Port.
newsitem.headline: NZ council mulls sell-down of Wellington Port.

text.p: The Wellington Regional Council may sell down its 76.9 percent shareholding in the Port of Wellington, possibly through a partial float on the stock exchange, within the next 12 months, council chairman Stuart Macaskill said on Tuesday.
"We expect with a degree of optimism that within the next 12 months we will move to a sell-down," Macaskill told Reuters.

The council would retain at least 51 percent of the shares, he said. A sale would be discussed with minority shareholder Manawatu-Wanganui Regional Council, and it was possible its 23.1 percent stake would be sold at the same time.
Macaskill said the port was worth in excess of NZ$50 million.
The port's last profit result was $2.05 million for the six months to December. Macaskill said profit for the full year would be "about five to six million".
He said the Port of Wellington's balance sheet was in good shape in comparison with most other New Zealand ports.
"It's up there with the top three or four in the country."
Any sale of the council's shares would take place after a decision had been made on where the Wellington ferry terminal would be.

Tranz Rail is looking at developing a new terminal either north of its current Kaiwharawhara terminal, on Tranz Rail land, or moving to Glasgow wharf opposite the Wellington Railway Station. A decision is likely within two months.
"If there is cemented an ongoing long-term business arrangement between Tranz Rail and the port company, that would make the port a more attractive prospect for investors," Macaskill said.
"If that transaction doesn't come off, it is obvious that the significant land holdings that the port company has may well produce other opportunities."
Macaskill said when the council last looked at the issue, it liked the option of a sharemarket float but would take advice from consultants.
